newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-AUSTRIA TO BID FOR EURO 2004 WITH HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRIA TO BID FOR EURO 2004 WITH HUNGARY.

text.p: The Austrian government on Tuesday pledged its full financial support for a joint bid to host the 2004 European soccer championship finals with neighbouring Hungary.
Chancellor Viktor Klima said the government would support the bid with 1.5 to two billion Austrian schillings ($123.3 million to $164.4 million).
"The government is backing the bid for the soccer championship," Klima told reporters after a weekly cabinet meeting.
The Austrian soccer federation (OeFB) had also negotiated with the Czech Republic, which shares a border with Austria, and Croatia.
OeFB press spokesman Heinz Palme said the Czechs had failed to present the required documents, while Croatia was turned down as it does not share a border with Austria.
Palme said the Austrian and Hungarian federations would meet in two weeks. The Hungarian government has already pledged financial support for the joint bid with Austria.
European soccer's governing body UEFA is expected to make a decision on bids in 1998. Spain is considered a leading contender.
Belgium and the Netherlands will be the first joint hosts in 2000.
